title: 2  Relations
text:
A relation records which ordered pairs from two sets are related.

Definition 2.1 (Relation) Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be sets. A relation over \(X \times Y\) is a subset \(R \subseteq X \times Y\).
If \(Y=X\), the relation is called homogeneous. When \((x,y)\in R\), we say that \(x\) is related to \(y\) and write \(xRy\).

The definition in Definition 2.1 treats a relation as a set of ordered pairs. Equivalently, its indicator is a proposition-valued function of two arguments.

title: 3  Set Identities
text:
Exercise 3.1 (De Morgan’s law for unions) For a sequence of sets \((A_i)_{i=1}^{\infty}\), show that
\[
\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i\right)^c
=
\bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i^c.
\]






TipSolution





We show equality by a chain of biconditionals. For arbitrary \(x\),
\[\begin{align*}
x \in \left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i\right)^c
&\iff x \notin \bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i \\
&\iff x \notin A_i \text{ for every } i\in\mathbb N \\
&\iff x \in A_i^c \text{ for every } i\in\mathbb N \\
&\iff x \in \bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i^c.
\end{align*}\]




This elementwise proof establishes the identity directly.

title: 4  Vector Spaces
text:
Exercise 4.1 (Double additive inverse) Prove that \(-(-v)=v\) for every \(v\in V\).






TipSolution





Let \(v\in V\). By definition, \(-v\) is an additive inverse of \(v\), so
\[
v+(-v)=0.
\]
Commutativity gives \((-v)+v=0\). But \(-(-v)\) is also defined by
\[
(-v)+(-(-v))=0.
\]
Because additive inverses are unique, \(-(-v)=v\).




The statement only uses the additive-group structure; no scalar multiplication is needed.
